---
title: "How Happy is the United States? 2019"
format: html
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
library(gt)

happiness <- read_csv("2019.csv")

us_rank <- happiness |> 
  filter(`Country or region` == "United States") |> 
  pull(`Overall rank`)
```

Is there a relationship between *economic power* and *happiness*? And how does the United States compare to other countries on these dimensions? In 2019, the United States was the `r us_rank`th happiest country in the world.

```{r}
ggplot(happiness, aes(x = `GDP per capita`, y = Score)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 3, color = "grey70") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Happiness vs GDP per Capita (2019)",
       subtitle = "World Happiness Report Data",
       x = "GDP per Capita",
       y = "Happiness Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12))
```

```{r}
happiness |> 
  slice_min(`Overall rank`, n = 10) |> 
  select(`Overall rank`, `Country or region`, Score, `GDP per capita`,
         `Social support`, `Healthy life expectancy`) |> 
  gt() |> 
  data_color(
    columns = Score,
    palette = "Greens",
    domain = range(happiness$Score)
  ) |> 
  tab_header(title = "10 Happiest Countries", subtitle = "World Happiness Report, 2019") |> 
  cols_label(
    `Overall rank` = "Rank",
    `Country or region` = "Country",
    `GDP per capita` = "GDP per Capita",
    `Social support` = "Social Support",
    `Healthy life expectancy` = "Life Expectancy"
  ) |> 
  fmt_number(columns = c(Score, `GDP per capita`, `Social support`, `Healthy life expectancy`), decimals = 2) |> 
  opt_stylize(style = 6, color = "green")
```
